newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus market lies low in weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus market lies low in weekly trade.

text.p: The Cypriot stock market appeared to show signs of recovery on Friday with gains of 0.38 percent after losses on previous trading days.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general index, which is set at 100 points, closed at 81.87 points on Friday after opening at 81.56.
The all-share index closed last Friday at 82.47, showing a weekly drop of 0.72 percent.

Theodoulos Charalambides of Laiki Investments attributed the drop, which he said was temporary, to public companies calling their dues on partly paid shares and new issues of the island's three largest banks expected until the end of the year.

"Funds have to be paid in partly-paid shares from now until the end of the year," said Charalambides. "Issues are expected from the Hellenic Bank, the Bank of Cyprus and the Popular Bank by the end of the year which will absorb around 60 million pounds ($27.6 million)," he said.
"That creates some pressure but I believe it is only temporary. I see the market fluctuating at these levels in the coming days but there will be an increase."
The banking sub-index closed at 88.60 points, shedding 0.90 points over Friday's close of 89.50.
Fully paid shares of the Bank of Cyprus closed unchanged at 339.5. Fully paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 312, down from 317.5 last week.
Hellenic Bank fully paid shares closed at 239 from 250 on Friday.
The tourist company sub-index closed at 75.32 from 74.44 last week, and the insurance company sub-index closed at 61.50 up from 60.09 last Friday.

Universal Life Insurance UNII.CY closed higher at 384.5, up 10.5 cents from last week. Paneuropean Insurance, closed at 136.5, unchanged from last week. Subsidiary Interamerican Insurance closed at 104.5 from 102.5 last week.
